images.name: The knot tied, untied, and kept tied
images.source: chain map: Binding, Fulfillment, and Release; Obligation as a Tied Structure; Lawful Release Without Rupture; Sanctuary as Held Conduct
images.scene: Cords are knotted between two parties. The one who tied them loosens some knots, keeps others fast for a set time, and forbids the other party to pick at them. At the end of the term the pilgrim's own knot is undone. The whole arrangement is sealed again as a rope-bound pact.

members.role: the knots: cord-ends bound together
the knotted thing as a binding compact
holding the knot to its full term, with nothing short
a knot undone by the one who tied it
the prohibition loosened, the thing released for use
the one who would untie what is still tied (game in ihram)
the pilgrim who has entered the tied state
the one who makes fast and firm
forbidden picking-open of God's sacred bonds
the inviolable right that must not be loosened
the pilgrim's own knot undone at the end of the term
the knot pulled tight (severity heard as tightness)
what stays tied and withheld
the question: which knots are undone?
a knot loosened in both directions between two peoples
a further prohibition-knot God does not wish to add
the knotted pact, confirmed
the rope that binds
the binding made fast between both sides

images.containment: The believers are told to fulfil their contracts, and the Arabic lets one hear knots: every أُحِلَّ is a knot that the one who tied it undoes, and every حُرُم is a knot he keeps fast.
images.perceptible: Halal (helal) and haram (haram) stop being two labels. They become two states of one cord: loosened and kept tied. The same ح ل ل that makes cattle lawful also names the pilgrim coming out of ihram (حَلَلْتُمْ), and 'do not violate' (لَا تُحِلُّوا۟) is literally 'do not untie'. The permission list is therefore itself part of the contract, and the reader who knows helal only as 'allowed' sees that it assumes a prior binding. The window opens with the knots (عقود) and closes the legal part with the pact that God knotted (ميثاق/واثقكم), so the whole passage is framed as one tied bond.

interactions.how: The cord is tied around a neck: the garland of the offering and the obligation 'put on the neck' (ق ل د B004) are knots of this same compact.
A knot is 'fulfilled' (أوفوا) when it holds to the full term; completion is the positive end of this tying.
The pilgrim's hands are tied from hunting while in ihram (غير محلي الصيد) and untied at حللتم فاصطادوا.
The window ends with the believers handing the matter over (توكل), the last movement of a bond whose holder is God.

images.movement: It is the frame of the window. What opens as 'fulfil the knots' comes back as 'remember His pact that He knotted with you'. In between, God shows which knots He loosens (food, game, marriage) and which He keeps (sanctuary, carrion, idolatrous slaughter).

images.name: The unmarked beast receives God's mark
images.source: chain map: Boundary Marks and Visible Restraint; The Marked Offering; A Bloodied Standing Stone Redirects Slaughter
images.scene: A plain, unmarked, speechless animal from the herd is set apart. It is garlanded at the neck, blood-marked at the hump and driven to the House, and at slaughter a name is spoken over it. Against this stand counterfeit marks: a voice raised for another than God, an erected stone as destination, arrows drawn to assign lots.

members.role: the unmarked, single-coloured animal with no sign on it
the living thing without discernment
the herd the animal comes from
marks of God, including the blood-mark cut on the offering's hump
the animal sent to the sanctuary
the neck-marker announcing 'this is an offering'
the destination
the protected zone around the destination
blood: a sign when drawn to mark the offering, forbidden when eaten
the counterfeit mark: the voice raised over the animal for another (the same act as the pilgrim's talbiya)
the counterfeit destination: the erected slaughter-stone
counterfeit signs: arrows drawn for lots
the name running on the tongue at the kill
(alternative root) the name as a brand-mark that makes the kill known as God's
the name as designation

images.containment: The verses list what may be eaten and which sanctities may not be violated, and the Arabic lets one hear an unmarked beast from the herd receiving a mark: a garland, a blood-sign, a spoken name.
images.perceptible: What decides the animal's status is the mark it carries and the voice spoken over it, and its species is secondary. بهيمة means by its root the unmarked, undistinguishing thing, and شعائر are marks. Between 5:1 and 5:4 the same animal can be marked for God (garland, hump-blood, 'mention God's name over it') or for another (أُهِلَّ لغير الله, the stone, the lots). The reader sees why the pilgrim's raised voice and the idolater's raised voice share one word (إهلال): the fault is in whom the voice is raised for.

interactions.how: The garland is the neck-cord of I3 seen as a sign; the strangling cord is its deadly double.
The counterfeit marks sit inside the list of deaths: the voice for another and the stone are 'modes of death' alongside strangling and falling.
The kill of the trained hound is lawful once God's name is set on it, so the mark completes the hunting scene.
The garlanded animal and the pilgrims (آمين) move toward the same House.

images.movement: It carries 5:1–5:4 from the herd to the House to the table, and turns the dietary list into a question of allegiance: whose mark does what you eat carry?

images.name: The cord around the neck
images.source: chain map: The Marked Offering; Sanctuary as Held Conduct
images.scene: A twisted cord goes around a neck. On the offering it is a garland of protection, on the strangled animal a noose of death, on the hunting dog a collar of training. A charm hung on the neck is the pagan version, and an obligation 'put on the neck' is the human version.

members.role: the cord twisted and wound
an obligation hung on one's own neck
the knot that fastens the cord
the throttled neck
the tight collar (the same word names a necklace and a dog-collar)
the throat opened at slaughter
the hung amulet (تميمة) of the old practice, heard beside the favour God has 'completed'
the trained, collared hunting dog

images.containment: The garlands, the strangled animal and the training of hounds are separate rulings, and the Arabic lets one hear one cord around a neck in all three.
images.perceptible: One object, the cord at the neck, takes three opposite meanings in three consecutive ayat: sanctuary (the garland), forbidden death (the noose) and trained service (the collar, as ق ل د and خ ن ق themselves name dog-collars). The reader feels that a bond is neither good nor bad in itself. What matters is who fastens it and toward what. The pact the believers carry (ق ل د B004) is this cord on their own necks.

interactions.how: It is the knot of I1 placed on a living body.
The garland is the protective mark; the noose is its reversal.
Strangling is the first of the forbidden deaths; the throat opened in ذبح is the lawful counterpart.
The collared hound is the neck-cord put to lawful use.

images.movement: A small hinge that joins the covenant knot (5:1) to the dietary list (5:3) and the hunt (5:4) through one physical object.

images.name: How the life went out: forbidden deaths and the completed slaughter
images.source: chain map: Captured Life and the Threshold of Edibility; Competing Modes of Death
images.scene: Animal bodies are listed by how they died: dead on their own, bled, choked, clubbed, fallen from a height, gored, half-eaten by a wild beast. Against these is the slaughter brought to completion while life is still in the animal. At the edge stands a starving man with an empty belly who does not lean toward the forbidden.

members.role: death without ritual slaughter
the blood that flows out
the meat
death by choking
death by a heavy blow
death by falling
death by goring
the prey another creature ate
the wild predator
slaughter brought to completion while life remains
the cut throat (here misdirected to the stone)
the empty belly of the one forced
compulsion
leaning off the straight line (which the compelled man does not do)

images.containment: The ayah names forbidden carcasses, and the Arabic lets one watch how each animal's life left it, with تذكية heard as a death brought to completion.
images.perceptible: The list is a series of deaths, not of foods: accident, violence, predation and neglect set against a deliberate, completed act done in the name of God (ذ ك و B003 'completion of slaughter'). The difference is between a life that was lost and a life that was taken back properly. The starving man 'not leaning' (متجانف) adds a bodily posture: need may bring him near the forbidden, but he does not incline toward it.

interactions.how: ذكاة is completion: the same ayah places 'you completed the slaughter' beside 'I completed your religion'.
The prey 'the wild beast ate' is forbidden; the prey the trained beast 'held for you' is lawful.
The deaths at the stone and under another's name are the counterfeit marks of I2.

images.movement: It gives 5:3 its bodily weight before the ayah turns to 'today': a religion is completed in the same breath as a slaughter is completed.

images.name: The trained hunter holds the prey for another
images.source: chain map: Captured Life and the Threshold of Edibility; The Trained Predator Holds for Another
images.scene: A hawk or hound, taught by a man who was taught by God, chases what resists capture, catches it, and holds it without eating so the master may eat. The pilgrim, meanwhile, holds his own hand back from the game until his state is loosened.

members.role: the prey that resists capture
the human hunter under restraint
the hunt released
(heard beside the hunt) the eagle, the raptor of the chase
the teaching that trains the animal
(heard beside جوارح) al-ʿallām, the falcon
the hunting animals
the animals that 'earn' for their owners
the trainer of hounds
God as the first teacher in the chain
the hound holding the prey and holding back its own hunger
the master eating

images.containment: The ayah permits game caught by trained animals, and the Arabic lets one see a chain of teaching and restraint: God teaches man, man teaches the hound, and the hound holds its catch for another.
images.perceptible: The ruling depends on restraint: the kill is lawful because the animal did not eat it and held it (أمسكن) for its master. This mirrors the pilgrim, who holds his hand back from game while in ihram. The Arabic word for hunting animals also means 'earners' (ج ر ح B002), so the hound works on its owner's behalf. A human being taught by God and passing the teaching down is how an appetite becomes lawful.

interactions.how: 'What the wild beast ate' against 'what they held for you': the same predator act is forbidden or lawful depending on training and restraint.
The hound's held mouth prefigures the enemy's held hand: God holds back in 5:11 as the hound holds back in 5:4.
The hunt is tied in ihram and untied at حللتم.
The catch becomes lawful once God's name is set on it.

images.movement: It turns law into formation. What is taught is restraint of appetite on another's behalf, and that is the ethic the window then asks of people under hatred (5:8).

images.name: The two good things: food and marriage, untied together
images.source: chain map: Intimacy as Fortification or Spillage; Marriage Builds an Enclosure; Uncontained and Secret Access
images.scene: A shared table between two peoples, and beside it a fortified household entered with a paid bride-gift. Outside it, water is poured out to be lost and a secret companion is kept. Nearby, an animal swells and dies from bad pasture.

members.role: 'the two good things', eating and marriage, named together
the wholesome as against the foul
the food tasted and shared
(heard beside the marriage clause) ḥalīl, the one who alights in the same dwelling: the spouse
the fortress whose inside cannot be reached
guarded chastity
the man who builds the enclosure by the marriage contract
the gift paid at the entrance
liquid poured out and lost
union with no contract
the secret companion of desire
(heard beside food) the belly swelling fatally from bad pasture
the work that comes to nothing

images.containment: The ayah allows the food of the People of the Book and marriage with chaste women, and the Arabic lets one hear 'the two good things', food and marriage, untied together.
images.perceptible: The dictionary itself pairs eating and marriage as al-aṭyabān, which explains why 5:5 moves without a break from table to marriage. Marriage becomes spatial: a walled enclosure (ح ص ن) entered through a paid gate, as opposed to water poured out on the ground (سفاح) or a hidden liaison (خدن). حبط keeps the food image to the end: a work 'swells and bursts' like an animal that grazed on bad pasture. This lets the reader see why disbelief ruins deeds from the inside.

interactions.how: Marriage is ع ق د, a knot tied; the enclosure is lawful because it is tied and paid.
ط ي ب runs on into 5:6: good food, good spouses, then 'good earth' for tayammum.
حبط and خاسرين are the short measure set against the full wage of 5:9.

images.movement: The 'today' of 5:3 goes on into 5:5: completion shows as an opened table and an opened household, both of them bounded.

images.name: The body cleansed: water down the limbs, earth when water fails
images.source: chain map: Purification Across Material Surfaces; Washing With Flowing Water; Clean Earth as a Transfer Medium
images.scene: A man rises toward prayer. Water runs over face, hands to the elbows and feet to the ankle-bones, and a wet hand passes over the head. He has come up from a low hollow in the ground, or is sick or travelling, or has touched a woman, and finds no water. He then goes to the clean surface of the earth, and a hand passes over face and hands. Nothing here is meant to trap him in a narrow, tangled place.

members.role: the body standing up
water made to flow, carrying dirt away
the face
the hands
a hand passed over, removing the trace
the protruding ankle-bones as the limit
the state that keeps one at a distance from prayer
full washing
the low hollow in the ground one comes up from
the absent water
the face of the earth, its surface
raised ground, the opposite of the hollow
earth as the means of cleansing from filth
the earthy hand passing over face and hands
the tangled thicket one cannot pass through
tightness, constriction
inner cleansing as the aim

images.containment: The ayah prescribes ablution and tayammum, and the Arabic lets one see a body coming up from a low hollow in the ground to the clean face of the earth, with a hand passing over it.
images.perceptible: The ayah has a vertical movement: the man comes up from al-ghāʾiṭ, the low hollow (the word for the privy is literally 'the depression'), and goes to al-ṣaʿīd, the raised, clean face of the earth. He stands (قمتم) facing prayer. The wet hand and the dusty hand (مسح) do the same work of 'passing over and removing the trace'. حرج pictures what God does not want: a thicket too dense to pass through, not merely an abstract 'difficulty'.

interactions.how: Tayammum means 'aiming': the same move as the pilgrims aiming at the House in 5:2.
ط ي ب: the good food and good spouses of 5:5 become good earth.
The hands washed and wiped for prayer are set against hands stretched out in aggression in 5:11.
Cleansing ends in 'to complete His favour upon you'.

images.movement: After what enters the body (food) and whom the body joins (marriage), the window cleanses the body to stand before God, so that permission ends in presence.

images.name: Setting one's face toward a goal
images.scene: Travellers head toward the House seeking bounty. A man rises and turns his face to prayer. A traveller without water aims deliberately at clean ground. At the end, justice is the step that brings one nearest to the goal of guardedness.

members.role: those aiming straight at the House
seeking
rising to undertake
the face as the direction one is intent on
being on the road
aiming deliberately at a chosen target
drawing nearer to the goal

images.containment: Pilgrims head to the House and worshippers do tayammum, and the Arabic lets one hear the same verb of aiming in both: the dictionary glosses آمّين البيت and التيمم with one sense.
images.perceptible: The Turkish reader knows teyemmüm only as a ritual with dust. The ء م م entry glosses it through 'those aiming at the Sacred House', and ي م م B001 is 'aiming a spear at one man rather than others'. Tayammum is a pilgrimage in small: the one who cannot reach water still sets out, deliberately, toward something clean. Justice in 5:8 is then described in the same spatial terms: 'nearer' to taqwa.

interactions.how: The garlanded offering and the pilgrims move toward the same House.
The aiming is carried out in the body: face, hands, earth.
Justice is measured as closeness to the goal (أقرب).

images.movement: It gives the window a direction. The rulings are not fences only but a road, and each prohibition and cleansing is a step toward the House or toward God.

images.name: The witness standing upright with the scale level
images.source: chain map: Justice Arrests Hostile Motion; Testimony Held to an Even Line
images.scene: A man stands erect as a witness holding a balanced scale, or loads two equal packs on a mount. Hatred of a people pulls at one side. Beneath it lies the harvest-like 'earning' that hatred would bring in: the transgression that runs past the boundary.

members.role: standing straight, level
upholding and giving full due
present and seeing
the level scale
equity
hatred as the weight on one pan
hatred 'earning' one a deed, pulling one into it
two loads balanced on either side of a mount
straightening a thing until it is level
the same pull, first appearance
running past the boundary
transgression as the thing not to cooperate in

images.containment: The believers are told to stand for God as witnesses in justice, and the Arabic lets one see an upright man holding a level scale while hatred pulls at one pan.
images.perceptible: Adl (adalet) here is a physical balancing: two packs on a camel must weigh the same or the animal falls (ع د ل B004), and a crooked thing is set straight (B005). Hatred is not forbidden as a feeling. What is forbidden is its pull on the scale, and يجرمنكم pictures it 'earning' a deed for you. The same warning appears twice (5:2, 5:8): first about the sanctuary, then about testimony.

interactions.how: The warning against being carried by hatred (5:2, 5:8) is answered by God's withholding the enemy's hand (5:11).
The hound holds back its appetite for its master; the witness holds back his hatred for God.
Justice is 'nearer' to taqwa.

images.movement: It moves the window from the ritual body to social conduct and shows that the restraint learned in ihram and hunting governs testimony against enemies.

images.name: Brought to full measure
images.source: chain map: Obligation as a Tied Structure
images.scene: A measure is filled to the brim, a weave finished, a slaughter completed, an udder full. Against them stands the short measure: a scale tipped to cheat, a belly swollen with bad fodder, a work that comes to nothing.

members.role: full measure given
the slaughter completed
completion of the religion
the favour brought to its end-point
the favour that fills
short measure, a tipped scale
work emptied out
favour completed again through cleansing
fullness overflowing (the udder full of milk)
the wage paid in full

images.containment: God completes religion and favour and promises a great reward, and the Arabic lets one hear a measure being filled to the brim, and beside it the short measure of those who lose.
images.perceptible: The window is full of completion words: وفاء, كمال, تمام, ذكاة, شكر. The believer's 'fulfil' (5:1) is answered by God's 'I completed' (5:3, 5:6). Gratitude (şükür) is heard as the fullness of an udder that runs over, so it is what completeness produces and not only a polite response. The 'losers' (hüsran) are those whose scale was short.

interactions.how: The knot held to its term is the knot 'fulfilled'.
ذكاة puts a completed slaughter next to a completed religion.
حبط/خاسرين close the marriage-and-food ayah with the empty measure.

images.movement: It is the window's axis: human fulfilment (أوفوا) and divine completion (أكملت/أتممت/ليتم) meet, and the wage of 5:9 is the measure filled.

images.name: The hand stretched out and the palm folded back
images.source: chain map: Justice Arrests Hostile Motion; The Withheld Hand
images.scene: A group resolves on violence and stretches its hands toward the believers. Another hand folds those hands shut and turns them back. The believers, whose own hands were washed for prayer and joined in helping one another toward good, hand their affair over to that holder.

members.role: the earlier turning-away, barring from the Mosque
hands joined in help
the resolve knotted in the soul
hands stretched out to seize
the hand as force
holding back, turning away
the palm, which grasps and which opens
closing and gathering in
handing one's affair over
the believers' own hands washed for prayer

images.containment: God recalls how He held back a people's hands, and the Arabic lets one see hands stretched out and folded back, and a palm, كف, that is both the hand and the holding back.
images.perceptible: كفّ is at once 'palm' and 'hold back': God's restraint is pictured as a hand closing over hands. Stretching (بسط) is the opposite of gripping (قبض), so the enemy's open reach is folded shut. The last word, توكل, is a handing-over, and the believers put their affair into that restraining hand. The same body part has been washed for prayer (5:6), joined in help (5:2) and stretched in hatred (5:11).

interactions.how: The believers are asked not to let hatred carry them into aggression (5:2, 5:8); God then restrains the aggressors' hands for them.
The hound 'held' (أمسكن) for its master; God 'held back' (كفّ) for His servants.
The pact of 5:7 is sealed with a handing-over (توكل): the one who ties the knots also holds the hands.

images.movement: It closes the window by turning the restraint God asked of the believers (from game, from transgression) into a restraint God exercises for them, and grounds trust in what was actually seen.

concepts.concept: Loosening that lets something settle into use: a knot undone, a ban lifted, a traveller alighting, a debt falling due, a spouse sharing one dwelling.
A thing, time, place or person withheld from use and so protected: the forbidden, the sanctuary, the sacred month, the pilgrim's state, the inviolable right.
Binding ends together so they hold: the physical knot, the compact, and the heart's firm resolve.
Firmness that can be leaned on: trust, tight fastening, the rope, and the confirmed pact.
An enclosed interior that cannot be reached: fortress, guarded chastity, the married state, the horse that shelters its rider.
Bringing something to its full pitch: slaughter completed, age reached, fire blazing up, mind sharpened.
Soft ease and good condition: favour, comfort, and livestock as the herder's well-being, so 'cattle' and 'favour' sit in one root.
What is agreeable and clean against the foul: wholesome things, cleansing oneself from filth, and 'the two good things', food and marriage.
A twisted cord laid on a neck: the cord itself, the marking garland, the sword-belt, and an obligation hung on someone.
The mother as source and direction, and aiming straight at a destination, which the dictionary also uses to gloss tayammum.
The palm as the organ that grips, and the act of holding back, closing in and gathering.
Level balance: fair judgment, two loads balanced on a mount, a thing set straight.
Standing upright: the erect body, rising to a task, upholding and giving full due, straightness.

movement: The window is framed by a tied bond. It opens with 'fulfil the knots' (عقود) and its legal part closes with 'remember the pact He knotted with you' (ميثاق/واثقكم). Inside that frame God shows which knots He loosens (أُحِلَّ: cattle, game after ihram, good food, the food and women of the People of the Book) and which He keeps tied (sanctuary, the sacred month, the marked offering, carrion and deaths under other names). Physical objects carry the move from law to formation. The unmarked beast (بهيمة) receives God's mark (garland, blood-sign, spoken name), and a single neck-cord can mean sanctuary, strangling or training. The trained hound holds its catch for another, and that teaches the restraint the window then asks of people: the pilgrim holds his hand from game, the witness holds his hatred off the scale. At the centre, 'today' three times joins divine completion to human fulfilment: the slaughter completed, the religion completed, the favour completed. Food and marriage are opened together as 'the two good things', and the body, cleansed from the low hollow to the clean face of the earth, is aimed at prayer as pilgrims aim at the House. The restraint asked of the believers in 5:2 and 5:8 is answered in 5:11 by the restraint God exercised for them: He folded back the hands stretched toward them. The window ends with the believers handing their affair to the one who ties, unties and holds.

plan.note: Show the three motions of one cord: tie (عقود), untie (أُحِلَّتْ), keep tied (غير محلي الصيد وأنتم حرم). Helal means 'untied', and God is the one who ties fast (يحكم). Introduce بهيمة as the unmarked, undistinguishing beast of the herd and أوفوا as full measure. Keep it light: the reader should only notice that 'lawful' assumes a knot.

'Do not violate' is 'do not untie' God's marks. Picture the offering animal marked by garland and hump-blood, driven with the pilgrims who are 'aiming at' (آمّين) the House. حللتم: the pilgrim's own knot is undone and the hunt reopens. Name the pull of hatred (شنآن, يجرمنكم) and running past the boundary (تعتدوا). Hands joined in help point ahead to 5:11. The eagle heard in العقاب may be mentioned lightly beside the hunt.

Read the list as a series of deaths: choked, clubbed, fallen, gored, half-eaten, against the slaughter 'completed' (ذكيتم). Set the counterfeit marks (voice raised for another, the erected stone, the lot-arrows) against the marks of 5:2. The strangling cord is the garland reversed. Then 'today': completion of slaughter, of religion, of favour. End with the starving man who does not lean toward the forbidden.

The chain of teaching (God, then man, then hound) and restraint (أمسكن: the hound holds the prey and its own hunger for another). What the wild beast ate is forbidden; what the trained beast held is lawful. God's name spoken over the kill is the mark that completes the beast's story. The collar links to the neck-cord.

'The two good things', food and marriage, are untied together, which is why the ayah moves from table to household. Marriage as a walled enclosure entered by a paid gift, against water poured out and the secret companion. حبط as a belly swollen from bad pasture, خاسرين as the short measure.

The body stands and turns its face to prayer. Water runs down the limbs. From the low hollow (غائط) to the raised, clean face of the earth (صعيد). Tayammum as 'aiming' (the same sense as آمّين البيت). حرج as a thicket God does not push you into. Favour completed again; gratitude as fullness overflowing.

The frame closes: the knots of 5:1 return as the pact God knotted with you, both a rope that binds and firmness to lean on. 'We heard and obeyed' is the believers' side of the tying. God knows what the breasts hold, where the resolve (ع ق د B006) is tied.

The witness stands upright with the scale level. Justice as two loads balanced on a mount and a crooked thing set straight. Hatred is allowed as a feeling but must not tip the pan. Justice is 'nearer' to taqwa. Point out that this repeats the warning of 5:2 in a new setting.
The wage paid in full is the measure filled, the answer to 'fulfil' in 5:1 and the opposite of the short measure of 5:5.
A short contrast: those who cover over and deny are bound as companions of the blaze. It needs no new image; let it sit as the far side of the pact and the wage.

Hands stretched to seize and a palm (كفّ) that folds them back: God's restraint shown as a hand. It answers the restraint asked of the believers in 5:2 and 5:8 and echoes the hound that 'held' in 5:4. توكل as handing one's affair over to the one who ties, unties and holds.

chains_set_aside.title: S14. A Bow Is Finished and Stress-Tested
chains_set_aside.why: Only م س ح B013 falls in this window (5:6), and nothing in the ablution ayah calls up a bow; the other members are outside the window.

chains_set_aside.title: S15. Seed Is Covered, Raised, and Ripened
chains_set_aside.why: Here ك ف ر B008 and ش ك ر B004 are isolated. The 'covering' of kufr is better served elsewhere in the surah, and no word in 5:1–11 supplies soil or crop roles.

chains_set_aside.title: S16. A Waterskin Is Stitched Leak-Tight
chains_set_aside.why: ك ل ب B006 and م س ك B005 in 5:4 are firmly held by the hunting scene. Hearing leather-stitching there would compete with the payoff and adds nothing.

chains_set_aside.title: S17. A Reservoir Directs and Retains Water
chains_set_aside.why: Its members here (م س ك B004, ء ت ي B004) are single and unactivated. أمسكن is fully used by I5.

chains_set_aside.title: S18. Milk Is Collected, Set, and Thickened
chains_set_aside.why: ق ل د B008 and ك ع ب B006 have no activator here. The one useful piece, ش ك ر B003 (fullness), is kept in I10.

chains_set_aside.title: S19. A Herd Takes Its Appointed Watering Turn
chains_set_aside.why: ق ل د B007 in 5:2 has no water context in this window. The rest of the chain is in later passages.

chains_set_aside.title: S20. Sorcery Works Through Knots and Diversion
chains_set_aside.why: ع ق د B013 would compete with the covenant knot of 5:1. The pagan-sign theme (lots, amulet) is carried more directly by ز ل م and ت م م B002 within I2 and I3.

chains_set_aside.title: S21. A Sale Is Ratified Palm to Palm
chains_set_aside.why: م س ح B017 and ل م س B004 are in 5:6, where the ablution and intimacy senses dominate. The handshake has no activator there.

chains_set_aside.title: S23. A Bloodied Standing Stone Redirects Slaughter
chains_set_aside.why: Not dropped: merged into I2 as the counterfeit destination (ن ص ب B002), with ش ع ر B006 blood-marking.

chains_set_aside.title: S24. A Wedding Moves From Contract to Household
chains_set_aside.why: ه د ي B006 (bride conveyed) in 5:2 is too far from the marriage clause of 5:5 to be heard. The household enclosure is carried by ح ص ن and ح ل ل B006 in I6.

chains_set_aside.title: S26. A Padded Garment Is Cut, Filled, and Hemmed
chains_set_aside.why: ك ف ف B004 (hem) in 5:11 is outweighed by palm/withholding, and no other member is in the window.

chains_set_aside.title: S30. A Weak-Hocked Mount Cuts Off the Journey
chains_set_aside.why: ح ل ل B014 and و ك ل B005 would work against the window's use of ح ل ل (untying) and توكل (handing over).

chains_set_aside.title: S32. Rain Descends, Travels, and Revives Ground
S33. A Hearth Pot Is Supported, Lowered, and Strained
chains_set_aside.why: ج ع ل B007 (pot-cloth) in 5:6 has no activator.

chains_set_aside.title: Boundary Marks and Visible Restraint — Sanctuary as Held Conduct (subchannel B)
chains_set_aside.why: Not dropped: split between I1 (sacred status as a knot kept tied) and I3 (the neck-cord).
